# min2phase: where it came from, and an unresolved licence contradiction

> **Resolved 2026-08-29 — by removal.** The question below was never answered; it was made
> moot. min2phase is gone from this repository: the app's engine is our own
> `apps/web/lib/two-phase.js`, written from Kociemba's published method
> (`dev-docs/two-phase-provenance.md`), and `cubing` is no longer a dependency of any kind.
> This note stays as the record of why — and as the caution: the claim "vendored min2phase is
> MIT" was made here once, on the evidence of a directory name, and was not supported.

`vendor/min2phase.js` WAS generated by `apps/web/vendor-min2phase.mjs` (both now deleted), which
copied one chunk out of the installed `cubing` package and patched its search bounds. This note
exists because the licence under which we shipped it **was not settled**, and it was vendored
before anyone checked.

Established 2026-08-29, all directly verifiable:

| | |
|---|---|
| Our artifact | `apps/web/vendor/min2phase.js` (gitignored, regenerated) |
| Sourced from | `cubing@0.63.3`, `dist/lib/cubing/chunks/search-dynamic-solve-3x3x3-*.js` |
| That chunk's own header | `// src/cubing/vendor/mit/cs0x7f/min2phase/3x3x3-min2phase.js` |
| `cubing`'s package licence | **`MPL-2.0 OR GPL-3.0-or-later`** |
| Licence files in `cubing.js` | `LICENSE-GPL.md`, `LICENSE-MPL.md` — **no MIT file** |
| Upstream `cs0x7f/min2phase` README | **"License GPLv3 — Copyright (C) 2023 Shuang Chen"** |

## The contradiction

cubing.js files min2phase under a directory named `mit/`. The upstream project states GPLv3.
There is no MIT text anywhere in either tree — not beside the file, not at `vendor/mit/`, not in
cubing's root.

The same mismatch applies to the other entries under `vendor/mit/cs0x7f/`: `cstimer`'s own
repository is GPL-3.0.

Three readings, and this note cannot choose between them:

1. Shuang Chen granted cubing.js a separate MIT licence for these files. Authors may licence the
   same code differently to different parties, and a systematic pattern across four directories
   points this way.
2. The directory name is stale — the vendored version predates the GPLv3 statement.
3. The directory name is simply wrong.

**A directory name is evidence of someone's classification, not a grant.** Until one of the three
is established, the safe assumption is the upstream statement: **GPL-3.0**.

## Why this matters here

This repository has no `LICENSE` file and is marked `private`, so its intended licence is
undeclared — and it is plainly built to be distributed (Tauri bundling, icons, a signing script).
GPL-3.0 obligations trigger on distribution, not on use. If min2phase is GPL-3.0, shipping it
makes the combined work GPL-3.0 on release.

That is precisely the question this project was weighing for *algorithm data*, where the ground
is softer because move sequences are arguably facts. Here it is **code**, where it is not soft at
all — and it was already vendored, on a recommendation that rested on a directory name.

## What would settle it

- Ask the cubing.js maintainers what grant `vendor/mit/` records, or find the commit that placed
  min2phase there and any accompanying statement.
- Ask Shuang Chen directly.
- Or remove the dependency: min2phase is not irreplaceable. The two-phase search could be written
  from Kociemba's published method, the same way `dev-docs/optimal-solver-plan.md` proposes for
  the optimal solver — with the same provenance discipline, and with the tiered search and its
  tests already in place to check any replacement against.

Until then: **do not distribute a release without resolving this**, and do not repeat the claim
that the vendored min2phase is MIT. It was made in this repository's notes and in commit
`3a9c73f`; it is not supported.
